court: In the High Court of Madras†
judges_raw: (Before G.K. Ilanthiraiyan and R. Poornima, JJ.)
respondents: State of Tamil Nadu Rep. by the Additional Chief Secretary to Government Home and Others
advocates: For Petitioner : Mr. R. Vinoth Bharathi
For Respondents : Mr. T. Senthil Kumar Additional Public Prosecutor
judgment_text:
Prayer : Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, to issue a writ of Habeus Corpus calling for the records connected with the detention order of the second respondent in No. 26/BCDFGISSSV/2025 dated 22-3-2025 and quash the same and direct the respondents to produce the detenu by name Sakthivel, son of Govindhasamy aged about 28 years now detained in Palayamkottai Central Prison before this Court and set him at liberty forthwith

The Order of the Court was delivered by

G.K. Ilanthiraiyan, J.:— The prayer in the petition is to quash the impugned order passed by the second respondent in No. 26/BCDFGISSSV/2025 dated 22-3-2025 and consequently direct the respondents to produce the detenu by name Sakthivel, son of Govindhasamy aged about 28 years now detained in Palayamkottai Central Prison before this Court and set him at liberty forthwith.

2. The petitioner is none other than the mother of the detenu. Challenging the very same detention order she already filed HCP(MD) No. 622 of 2025 and raised the following grounds:

“G. That the several pages are in the booklet in English, the detaining authority did not supplied the Tamil version of the said pages, the detenu and his family members did not able to understand the said pages in the booklet. Therefore the detenu was not able to effectively represent his case before the Advisory Board. Therefore the detenu sent the representation to Respondent 1 through Respondent 3 and seeking the Tamil ranslated to the said page to the detenu. But the same was not considered expeditiously.

H. That the several pages of Tamil and English version of the booklet and rounds of detention differ, it confuses the detenu and therefore the detenu did not able to prefer effective representation before the authorities. It clearly established that the detaining authority mechanically passed the detention order without applying his mind and without perused the documents available in the booklet. That the detaining authority failed supply all documents relied in the detention Order.

I. That the detenu and his family members were not able to read understand the legal and technical words in the grounds of detention and the booklet. Therefore the detenu was not able to effectively represent his case before the Advisory Board. Therefore the petitioner sent the representation to Respondent 1 and they represent him to permit his advocate for the represent his case before the Advisory Board, but the same was not considered expeditiously”

3. All the above grounds were considered by this Court and the HCP(MD) No. 622 of 2025 was dismissed by this Court by an order dated 17-11-2025.

4. Now the petitioner has filed the second Habeus Corpus Petition challenging the very same detention order.

5. Thus it is clear that the detenu can agitate fresh ground on the second petition though available to him on the earlier occasion not taken. In the case on hand, as stated above, all the grounds raised by the petitioner before this Court, while challenging the detention order dated 22-3-2025, were considered by this Court and the petition was dismissed by an order dated 17-11-2025.

6. On perusal of the ground raised in the first Habeus Corpus Petition in Grounds G.H. and I, the petitioner has raised the very same grounds. Therefore this Court has no hesitation in holding that the second Habeus Corpus Petition challenging the same detention order is maintainable only if the grounds taken in the second Habeus Corpus Peition were not available to the detenue at the time of filing or adjudication of the first Habeus Corpus Petition. However, in respect of the grounds which were available while instituting the first Habeus Corpus Petition and not taken by the detenue, the same will not provide any assistance for filing a second Habeus Corpus Petition. In clear terms the second Habeus Corpus Petition is maintainable only if the grounds taken in the second Habeus Corpus petition were not available to the detenue at the time of filing or adjudication of the first Habeus Corpus Petition and in no other circumstances the second Habeus Corpus Petition is maintainable. Therefore, this Court finds no ground to entertain the second Habeas Corpus petition as maintainable.

7. In view of the same, this petition is dismissed as not maintainable.
